fr_statement: Quoin SHALL implement its Quire adapter, validators, semantic and completeness analysis, configuration, plugin, module and catalog behaviour in Rust crates reached through the `quoin-core` boundary, preserving one catalog and one module store.
ac_id: FR-099 (bare FR trace, no AC cited)
ac_text: No row in FR-099's Acceptance Criteria table names `quire.coverage` or the obligation-projection behaviour this test checks (the twelve ACs cover validators.run, quire.validate, catalog.list, reconcile, manifest reading, semantic/completeness parity, skill tests, ix-cli-core imports, workflow-assets disposition, the ix-flow child process, partial-module refusal and duplicate-type folding). The Trace tag names only the bare FR, so no AC-level text exists to quote; the Description SHALL sentence above is shown instead as the nearest normative text.
note: Looks solid on its own terms: it exercises the real absent-key serialisation rule (target_ids/parameters dropped rather than emitted empty) and the field mapping, not just a no-panic smoke test. But the trace tag is FR-level only (bare 'FR-099') and none of FR-099's 12 ACs actually describes `quire.coverage`'s behaviour, so a reviewer cannot check this test against a specific acceptance criterion at all -- only against the FR's general intent.

fr_statement: Given the frozen audit snapshot, the audit SHALL inventory every default module, declared semantic type, contract surface, and Markdown document without silently excluding malformed or untyped input.
ac_id: FR-052-CON-3 (a Constraint, not an Acceptance Criterion)
ac_text: FR-052 has no CON-3; its constraints are two unlabelled bullets ('Files explicitly excluded... remain in the document denominator'; 'A parser failure is evidence; it SHALL NOT abort enumeration'). FR-052 as a whole is about inventorying the default-module corpus (module/type/document counts for a semantic-type audit) and has nothing to do with `quire.properties`' shape-map keying, which is what this test actually checks. The Trace tag appears to point at the wrong requirement entirely.
note: The test itself is a solid, specific assertion of the row_id-keying and skip-on-no-id behaviour in `properties()`. But the Trace tag names FR-052-CON-3, which is neither an AC nor a constraint that exists under that id, and FR-052 (module-corpus inventory audit) is a different subsystem entirely from the quire boundary this file tests -- a clear trace-tag mismatch that a naive AC-matches-test check would not catch.

fr_statement: Quoin SHALL expose the implemented FR-063 record, FR-064 attestation, retained output intake, and FR-065 receipt contracts through supported `quoin change-assurance` commands.
ac_text: `schema` lists the three normative asset names and emits each by name byte-identically to the packaged asset; an unknown name is refused with exit 2.
note: Looks solid: it asserts byte-identity against the actual compiled-in constant (`quoin_change_assurance::schemas::PROOF_ATTESTATION_V1`), which is exactly what AC-8's 'byte-identically to the packaged asset' clause requires, and the assertion would fail if `schema()` re-serialised or truncated the asset.

fr_statement: Quoin SHALL expose the implemented FR-063 record, FR-064 attestation, retained output intake, and FR-065 receipt contracts through supported `quoin change-assurance` commands.
ac_text: `schema` lists the three normative asset names and emits each by name byte-identically to the packaged asset; an unknown name is refused with exit 2.
note: Solid: checks the exact BadRequest code, the op name, the offending name echoed back, and that the refusal enumerates the actually-shipped names -- directly backing the 'refused with exit 2' half of AC-8 (exit 2 itself is asserted elsewhere at the CLI layer, not here, so this test only covers the error-shape half).

fr_statement: When a caller selects `fan-out`, `change-impact`, or `churn`, `quoin` SHALL derive one deterministic `GraphAnalysisReport` from a validated Quire assurance export, the retained evidence store, and the existing auditor verdicts.
ac_text: Fan-out reports each suite once with the exact sorted set and count of distinct live obligations; duplicate symbols and duplicate `(suite, obligation)` entries do not increase the count.
note: Looks thinner than the AC promises: it checks one suite's obligation count is 1, but never plants a duplicate symbol or a duplicate (suite, obligation) entry to prove de-duplication -- the specific claim AC-1 makes ('duplicate ... entries do not increase the count') is asserted only by `analyze_fan_out`'s use of a `BTreeSet` here, not by an adversarial case in this particular test. The de-dup claim may well be covered by a sibling test not selected into this corpus.

fr_statement: For `change-impact`, an optional repeated `--relation` selection. When absent, the exact default is `depends_on`, `derives_from`, `implements`, `mitigates`, `refines`, `requires`, `satisfies`, and `traces_to`; an explicit selection replaces rather than extends that default.
ac_text: Change impact records its default or replacement relationship-kind selection, computes the reverse transitive dependency closure from every requested requirement, terminates on cycles, retains shared dependents, and selects the lexicographically first shortest path deterministically.
note: Looks solid for the narrow slice of AC-3 it targets (None vs Some([]) are different answers), and it is a real behavioural assertion, not a tautology -- but it covers only the default-vs-empty distinction, not the closure/cycle-termination/shortest-path clauses the same AC also makes; a reader matching this single test against the full AC-3 text would overcredit it.

fr_statement: An absent or unreadable `--export`, `--premises`, or `--audit` path SHALL fail before row construction and name the failed input.
ac_text: Invalid inputs, absent or unreadable required `--export`/`--premises`/`--audit` paths, rejected premises, and mismatched audit identity fail before rows; absent, unreadable, incomplete, and empty retained inputs produce distinct report states and reasons, never an invented healthy zero.
note: Solid: directly exercises the required() naming-the-input path inside load_graph_analysis_input for a missing audit.json, checking both the exit code and the QGA-1001 error code that identifies the failed input by name -- a specific, falsifiable slice of AC-9 (the 'absent ... --audit path' clause).
mutation_method: excluded: `Result<GraphAnalysisInput>` has no safe default to construct without deep type exploration, out of proportion for a sampled subset

fr_statement: Quoin SHALL keep a replaced path until its Rust replacement passes locally at the same candidate revision across differential, property and, for store-backed capabilities, digest-replay evidence.
ac_text: Removal is refused unless the retained and Rust paths both pass at the same candidate revision and the direct invocation already dispatches to the Rust interface.
note: Looks solid on the merits -- it exercises every branch of `Intake::of` including non-string and non-object `record_type` values, and separately checks `limit()` -- but the AC it is pinned to (AC-2, about removal being refused absent same-revision parity evidence) is a process/removal-gating criterion that has nothing to do with the intake classifier itself; this test is better read as generic Rust-port coverage than as evidence for AC-2's specific claim.
mutation_method: excluded: two symbols (`Intake::of`/`Intake::limit`) pinned to one triple, and the corpus author separately flagged the Trace tag as not matching either method's own behaviour

ac_text: Removal is refused unless the retained and Rust paths both pass at the same candidate revision and the direct invocation already dispatches to the Rust interface.
note: Looks solid and well-constructed (an explicit anti-vacuity floor pins the case count to 4), and it does exercise the real `bound_field` refusal path across four distinct routes, but again the AC it cites (AC-2, same-revision removal gating) has no semantic connection to field-size ceilings -- another instance of the FR-101-AC-2 tag being used as a generic 'this backs the Rust port' marker rather than a claim about this AC's text.

fr_statement: Quoin SHALL delete a replaced implementation and the tests covering it in the same change, and deletion SHALL be the final step for that capability.
ac_text: `make lint` and `make test` pass at the candidate revision with no observable behaviour change recorded by the command-surface snapshot.
note: Looks vacuous: `quoin-core`'s `MAX_RECORD_ID_BYTES` is DEFINED as `quoin_measurement::MAX_RECORD_ID_BYTES` (see symbol_body), so this assert_eq compares the constant to itself by construction and can never fail regardless of what either crate's real ceiling is -- it documents an intentional aliasing decision but proves nothing at runtime. It also has no real bearing on AC-7's 'make lint/test pass with no observable behaviour change' claim.
mutation_method: excluded: a re-exported constant, not a function; 'stub returning a default' does not apply, and the test's own vacuity (asserting a value against its own re-export) needs a different mutation than a body stub

fr_statement: Quoin SHALL retain each replaced TypeScript, JavaScript, MJS or Python implementation until its Rust replacement is demonstrated equivalent at one candidate revision, then cut over the direct invocation in a reversible change, and only afterwards delete the replaced path together with its tests.
ac_text: Every first-party executable-path row records one current state and one final disposition, and the gate fails when a row is unclassified.
note: The test genuinely exercises real logic in `audit()` -- the `Option`-preserving `request.accepted.as_ref().map(...)` line is precisely what makes `reported` absent when no baseline was supplied, and the assertion would fail if that were collapsed to `unwrap_or_default()`. But AC-1's text is about the executable-path disposition matrix (a completely different subsystem than obligation auditing), so the trace tag does not actually describe what this test verifies.

fr_statement: Quoin SHALL retain each replaced TypeScript, JavaScript, MJS or Python implementation until its Rust replacement is demonstrated equivalent at one candidate revision, then cut over the direct invocation in a reversible change, and only afterwards delete the replaced path together with its tests.
ac_text: Every first-party executable-path row records one current state and one final disposition, and the gate fails when a row is unclassified.
note: Solid, end-to-end: it derives a real baseline from `baseline()`, feeds it back through `audit()`, and checks the ratchet actually suppresses the exact finding it accepted -- a genuine round-trip test of `ratchet`'s filtering, not a self-written fixture. As with GAP-11, the AC-1 trace tag (executable-path disposition matrix) does not describe this auditor-ratchet behaviour.

fr_statement: Quoin SHALL record the cutover of a capability's direct invocation as its own change, separate from the change that deletes the replaced path, and SHALL demonstrate that reverting the cutover restores the retained invocation.
ac_text: Reverting a cutover change restores the retained invocation, and comparing the evidence and accepted-corpus trees before and after the revert finds zero changed bytes.
note: The test itself is real: it plants a misspelled field (`acceptd`) and an undeclared extra field, and relies on `deny_unknown_fields` (via serde) inside the type `read` deserialises into to produce a BadRequest rather than silently dropping the field. But AC-3's actual text is about reverting a cutover and comparing evidence/corpus byte trees -- entirely unrelated to request-field strictness, so the trace tag is again a mismatch.
mutation_method: excluded: `read<T>` is generic with no `T: Default` bound, so no default value of the deserialised type can be constructed

fr_statement: Quoin SHALL record the cutover of a capability's direct invocation as its own change, separate from the change that deletes the replaced path, and SHALL demonstrate that reverting the cutover restores the retained invocation.
ac_text: Reverting a cutover change restores the retained invocation, and comparing the evidence and accepted-corpus trees before and after the revert finds zero changed bytes.
note: Vacuous: this literally re-states the constant's own literal value (32 * 1024 * 1024) back at itself, so it can only fail if someone edits the constant without updating the test in the same edit -- a change-detector, not a behavioural check. It also has no connection to AC-3's cutover-revert claim; a doubly weak entry.
mutation_method: excluded: a constant, same reasoning as GAP-10

fr_statement: Quoin SHALL keep a replaced path until its Rust replacement passes locally at the same candidate revision across differential, property and, for store-backed capabilities, digest-replay evidence.
ac_id: FR-101 (bare FR trace, no AC cited)
ac_text: No AC in FR-101's table is specific to `catalog.methods`'s first-wins method projection; the Trace tag names only the bare FR. Closest by theme is AC-2 ('Removal is refused unless the retained and Rust paths both pass at the same candidate revision...'), quoted for reference, though it does not describe this test's behaviour either.
note: Looks weak/vacuous for what its own doc-comment claims: 'uses the granted first-wins projection', but the test's `MethodCatalogFixture` (a test double implementing `CatalogHost`) hands back an ALREADY-MERGED, hand-written JSON blob directly -- the assertion only checks that `methods()` passes that canned payload through unchanged. The real first-wins merge logic lives inside the production `CatalogHost` implementation and `quoin-catalog`, neither of which this test reaches; it is effectively a passthrough smoke test wearing the name of the behaviour it does not exercise.

fr_statement: Quoin SHALL keep a replaced path until its Rust replacement passes locally at the same candidate revision across differential, property and, for store-backed capabilities, digest-replay evidence.
ac_id: FR-101 (bare FR trace, no AC cited)
ac_text: No AC in FR-101's table addresses catalog duplicate-module suppression before semantic reading; the Trace tag names only the bare FR. FR-099-AC-3/AC-12 (catalog duplicate-type handling) are the closest analogues in a sibling FR, not FR-101 itself.
note: Looks solid: the `RejectIgnoredSemanticFixture` used by this test actively asserts (via `assert_ne!`) that its `read_module` is never called with the suppressed module's root -- so the test really does prove the `if !retained_roots.contains(...) { continue; }` guard in `load()` skips semantic reading for the ignored duplicate, not merely that the response looks right by accident.

fr_statement: Quoin SHALL consume a validated `clause-binding-v1` report and partition every binding clause into direct evidence, an approved disposition, or open work.
ac_text: The consumer validates input against the pinned `clause-binding-v1` schema before using it.
note: Looks solid, and unusually well-grounded: the production type itself carries its own 'Trace: FR-046-AC-1' doc comment naming the exact pattern it replaces (`^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$`), and the test plants a value that fails that pattern ('sha256:not-a-digest') and checks it surfaces as BadRequest through `Deserialize` -- a genuine, specific proof of AC-1's schema-validation claim rather than a coincidence.

The AC-2 trace (same-revision removal gating) is unrelated to what this test verifies, though, so the tag itself is again a loose 'Rust port' marker.

note: Looks solid: it plants one well-formed and one structurally malformed record (missing required fields) in two different suites and checks both that the malformed one is skipped-and-named AND that the well-formed sibling still comes through -- directly exercising the `Err(EvidenceError::StoreRead) => skipped.push(path)` branch in `read_all` rather than only the happy path.

fr_statement: When a retained test is to be deleted, Quoin SHALL first restate every acceptance criterion that test carried on a tracking-tagged Rust test that fails when its property is violated.
ac_text: For each deleted test, the criterion it carried resolves to a tracking-tagged Rust test, and mutating the corresponding Rust source makes that test fail.
note: Looks solid for the vacuity half: it plants a scan with `rulesEvaluated: 0` and checks it lands in `vacuous_scan_suites` via the real `scan_is_vacuous` filter inside `audit_inputs`. The independence assertion is weaker -- it only checks that `independence` is empty when no `independence_policy` was supplied at all, which is true almost by construction (`map_or_else(Vec::new, ...)`) rather than proving anything about how independence is actually assessed when a policy IS present.

fr_statement: Quoin SHALL record the cutover of a capability's direct invocation as its own change, separate from the change that deletes the replaced path, and SHALL demonstrate that reverting the cutover restores the retained invocation.
ac_text: Reverting a cutover change restores the retained invocation, and comparing the evidence and accepted-corpus trees before and after the revert finds zero changed bytes.

fr_statement: When a retained test is to be deleted, Quoin SHALL first restate every acceptance criterion that test carried on a tracking-tagged Rust test that fails when its property is violated.
ac_text: For each deleted test, the criterion it carried resolves to a tracking-tagged Rust test, and mutating the corresponding Rust source makes that test fail.
note: Looks solid: it starts from an EMPTY store (so no binding can match), calls `affirm_binding`, and checks both `found: false` in the payload and that the store's path list is still empty afterward -- directly proving the `if outcome.found { write_bindings(...) }` guard actually skips the write rather than merely returning the right JSON while writing anyway.

fr_statement: When a retained test is to be deleted, Quoin SHALL first restate every acceptance criterion that test carried on a tracking-tagged Rust test that fails when its property is violated.
ac_text: For each deleted test, the criterion it carried resolves to a tracking-tagged Rust test, and mutating the corresponding Rust source makes that test fail.

fr_statement: The vocabulary is read, never minted... the values come from the same declaration the engine reads. (See also FR-037-CON-1: quoin SHALL NOT mint a vocabulary; values come from the artifact type's frontmatter schema.)
ac_text: The vocabulary's values are read from module data, not minted.
note: Reasonably solid but narrow: it checks one manifest's declared `frontmatter_schema_ref` comes back, which supports 'read from module data' in spirit, but does not itself prove the 'not minted' half of AC-1 (no adversarial case shows a hardcoded/fallback list being rejected). It is a single happy-path case, not a proof against the anti-pattern the AC exists to rule out.

fr_statement: A bundle whose module set declares no vocabulary has not been assessed. Reporting PASS over it is the green-matrix-over-dead-links result this program was created to stop... it fails only under --strict.
ac_text: A bundle with no declared vocabulary reports `UNCHECKED`, never `PASS`.
note: Looks solid and directly on point: it drives a real bundle through `assess_bundle` end to end (one NFR claiming one of two enum values -> CONDITIONAL, with the unowned value named) and separately proves the zero-vocabulary case returns UNCHECKED rather than PASS -- the exact distinction AC-12 (not the AC-1 also implied by the bare 'FR-037' half of the tag) is about, hitting the `vocabularies_checked == 0` branch in `verdict_for` directly.
